task_brief: Day 5 of "Professional Practice, Rights, and Pathways" (unit 2, grade 12) is a second concept model on arts careers and postsecondary pathways. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Assemble professional practice materials with a rights and licensing plan and a pathway action plan, timed to real application and audition deadlines. Today's work contributes to that by handling arts careers and postsecondary pathways at the concept model b stage, against the unit's wider topics of copyright licensing and contracts, pricing commissions and compensation, portfolio and application materials, and auditions interviews and submissions. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Study a second, contrasting model work for arts careers and postsecondary pathways and set it beside the first one you examined earlier in this unit. Build a comparison naming one choice the two makers share and one place they clearly diverge, with the effect of each difference described in terms a listener or viewer could verify. Then make one short study of your own that borrows the second maker's approach to arts careers and postsecondary pathways. Cite both works. Anything you did not make yourself must be public domain, openly licensed, or properly attributed. Use the attached Model A recap and contrasting Model B as the two works for comparison; no earlier source file is required. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about arts careers and postsecondary pathways, and it belongs to "Professional Practice, Rights, and Pathways", which also covers separate topics such as copyright licensing and contracts. Close out with this check before you stop: State what the contrasting example of arts careers and postsecondary pathways revealed that the first one did not. At grade 12 the bar is portfolio-quality independent work you could defend to an outside reader: intent stated, method justified, limitations named honestly, and revision traceable.

MODEL B — Contrast record for "One Clear Route." Intent: make a viewer follow one path. Two thumbnails were rejected because three equal paths weakened the message. The final uses one continuous line and empty space. Statement: "I removed two paths after checking whether a reader could name the focal route in five seconds." Compare this evidence-first decision with Model A. Use it to study arts careers and postsecondary pathways; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

critique_criteria: One shared choice and one clear divergence between the two model works are both named.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

remediation: Reteaching for arts careers and postsecondary pathways follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for arts careers and postsecondary pathways, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to arts careers and postsecondary pathways works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of arts careers and postsecondary pathways, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking arts careers and postsecondary pathways mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply arts careers and postsecondary pathways under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on arts careers and postsecondary pathways rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
